newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end higher, crown flat vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end higher, crown flat vs mark.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended higher on Friday with the long end of the market rising on strong U.S. industrial production data.
The crown weakened against the dollar but remained stable against the mark.

The market shrugged off Swedish employment figures, which showed the unemployment rose to 8.7 percent in December, while analysts had expected 8.1 percent. * Six-month T-bill rate rises one basis point to 3.70 pct. * Nine-year bond yield gains four basis points to 6.59 pct. * The crown is stable at 4.3570 a mark vs 4.3550 on Thursday
STOCKHOLM, Jan 17 (Reuter) - Swedish bond yields ended higher on Friday on strong U.S. industrial production data.
The crown remained stable against the mark, ending the day at 4.3570 a mark compared with 4.3550 late on Thursday.

"We have seen some interest in selling crowns abroad, largely stemming from Moody's decision to upgrade Finland's ratings but not Sweden's. But domestically there was buying interest so the market is fairly stable," one dealer said.
The nine-year bond yield rose four basis points to 6.59 percent, while the six-month T-bill rose one to 3.70 percent.
The spread with Germany stayed at 83 basis points and dealers described trade as quiet.
Next week market players will focus on the Riksbank's repo announcement and Swedish CPI, both due out Tuesday morning.
Economists expect a cut of between 15 and 20 basis points, from the current level of 4.10 percent, according to a Reuter poll.
